courses.title: Technical Skills Practicum
courses.description: Engineering graphics, spatial visualization, CAD, equation solvers, machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting, elements of engineering science. [1-3-3]. Prerequisite: All of APSC 160, MATH 100, MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170 and one of BMEG 102, PHYS 159 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL 112, WRDS 150. Corequisite: MECH 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Science I
courses.description: Rigid body kinetics and kinematics, basic electrical circuits, work and power, stress and strain, torsion, bending, engineering materials, probability and statistics. This course includes the content of ELEC 203. [11-2-1] Prerequisite: All of MATH 100, MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170; and one of BMEG 102, PHYS 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL 112, WRDS 150. Corequisite: All of MECH 220, MECH 224. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MATH 100, MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 170; and one of BMEG 102, PHYS 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL 112, WRDS 150

courses.title: Engineering Science II
courses.description: Fluid properties, equations of state. Pressure, buoyancy, hydrostatic forces. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. Work and heat; internal energy and enthalpy. Bernoulli's equation. Dimensional analysis, modelling. Turbulent flow in pipes; turbomachinery. Second law and the Carnot cycle; entropy; first and second law analysis of systems. [5-2-1]. Prerequisite: MECH 220. Corequisite: MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process
courses.description: Design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design projects representing both mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems. [3-8-0]. Prerequisite: MECH 220. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Integration of Engineering Concepts I
courses.description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on dynamics, solid mechanics, materials, electronics, and mathematics. [1-0-1]. Corequisite: MECH 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Integration of Engineering Concepts II
courses.description: Integration of the theory and practice of Mechanical Engineering to illustrate the commonality and conceptual connectivity of seemingly different technical areas. Emphasis on thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and mathematics. [1-0-1]. Corequisite: MECH 222. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
courses.description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design reports, business correspondence, verbal, online, and visual presentation of technical material. Restricted to students in the second year of Mechanical Engineering. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 226 or MECH 227. [1-0-1;1-0-1] Prerequisite: ENGL 112, WRDS 150, or APSC_O 176. Corequisite: All of MECH 220, MECH 221, MECH 222, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

coreq.text: All of MECH 220, MECH 221, MECH 222, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225

courses.title: Approaches to Technical Communication for Mechanical Engineers
courses.description: Written and oral communication. Preparation of design, business correspondence, verbal, online and visual presentation of technical material. Focus on the linguistic structure and style of technical communication. Restricted to students in Mechanical Engineering. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 226 or MECH 227. [3-0-4]. Prerequisite: MECH 220 and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL 112, WRDS 150. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

Corequisite: MECH 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.description: Machine shop practice, electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting. [0-2-2] Prerequisite: MECH 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

[2-0-0] Prerequisite: All of APSC 160, MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 158, PHYS 170; and one of APSC 100, APSC 150, APSC 151; and one of BMEG 102, PHYS 159; and one of APSC_O 176, ENGL 112, WRDS 150. Corequisite: MECH 221. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to the Mechanical Design Process II
courses.description: Intermediate design methodology, synthesis and analysis. Design project representing mechanical mechanism design and thermofluid systems. [1-8-0] Prerequisite: MECH 232. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Technical Skills Practicum IIA
courses.description: Electronic circuit construction and troubleshooting. [0-1-1]. Prerequisite: MECH 230. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Technical Skills Practicum IIB
courses.description: Machine shop practice. [0-1-1]. Prerequisite: MECH 234. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Statically determinate frames and trusses; normal and shear stresses and strains; shear force and bending moment diagrams; theory of beam bending, torsion of circular rods; transformation of stress and strain in two and three dimensions, Mohr's circle; yield and ultimate failure criteria. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of MATH 101, PHYS 170 or (b) all of APSC_O 172, APSC_O 173, APSC_O 180. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) all of MATH 101, PHYS 170 or (b) all of APSC_O 172, APSC_O 173, APSC_O 180

courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Fluid properties; statics; kinematics, dynamics, energy, and momentum principles for control volumes; dimensional analysis and similarity; laminar and turbulent flow; pipe flow; principles of centrifugal pumps. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: All of MATH 152, PHYS 170 and one of MATH 217, MATH 253; and either (a) PHYS 131 and one of PHYS 108, PHYS 118; or (b) PHYS 153 or (c) all of PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 159. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MATH 152, PHYS 170 and one of MATH 217, MATH 253; and either (a) PHYS 131 and one of PHYS 108, PHYS 118; or (b) PHYS 153 or (c) all of PHYS 157, PHYS 158, PHYS 159

courses.title: Data Analysis and Mechanical Engineering Laboratories
courses.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. [3-5-1*] Prerequisite: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225

courses.title: Data Analysis and Mechatronics Laboratories
courses.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials and heat transfer. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. Common mechanical devices. For students in the Mechatronics Option only. [3-3*-1*] Prerequisite: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225

courses.title: Machine Design
courses.description: Selection of flexible drives, bearings, fluid power system components, and couplings. Design of shafts, bolted joints and power screws. Design and selection of gears, gear trains, and mechanisms. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 360. [3-0-3]. Prerequisite: One of MECH 223, MECH 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Thermodynamics II
courses.description: Air standard and vapor cycles; first and second law of cycles. Exergy. Gas mixtures. Energy conservation. Equilibrium. Reacting systems. Application to thermofluid systems such as power plants. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280

courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Design Project
courses.description: Applying the design process, making educated assumptions and decisions, and working in teams to provide a new mechanical design. Weekly lecture discussing product development and various factors affecting the design. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher in Mechanical Engineering. [1-4-1] Prerequisite: MECH 223. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Materials for Mechanical Design
courses.description: Selection of material properties for mechanical design. Metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites and other hybrid materials. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 224 or (b) all of APSC 278, MECH 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 224 or (b) all of APSC 278, MECH 260

courses.title: Engineering Analysis
courses.description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing emphasized. [3-1-0]. Prerequisite: All of MECH 224, MECH 225. Equivalency: MATH 358. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Computational Methods for Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Computational methods for solving mechanical engineering problems. Numerical computation of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations; interpolation and extrapolation; numerical integration and differentiation; numerical solution of differential equations. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 358 or MECH 359. [3-1-1] Prerequisite: All of MECH 224, MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Beam deflections, singularity functions; use of tabulated solutions; column buckling; Castigliano's theorem, statically indeterminate beams, bending of beams with asymmetric cross-sections, shear centre; principal stresses and stress invariants in three dimensions. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: One of MECH 224, MECH 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Modelling of Mechatronic Systems
courses.description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, thermal, fluid elements and mixed mechatronic systems. Signal processing, signal conditioning. Sensors, data acquisition systems, actuators. [2-2-0] Prerequisite: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MECH 220, MECH 223, MECH 224, MECH 225

courses.title: Engineering Measurements and Instrumentation
courses.description: Industrial measurement needs including: architecture of electronic instrumentation systems; electrical representation of physical quantities; sensors and actuators; analog signal processing using linear and non-linear circuits; computer-based readout including programming for user-interface and data acquisition. [2-3-1] Prerequisite: Either (a) two of MECH 220, MECH 224, ELEC 203 or (b) all of MANU 230, ELEC 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) two of MECH 220, MECH 224, ELEC 203 or (b) all of MANU 230, ELEC 203

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Steady and transient conduction. Radiation heat transfer. Convective heat and mass transfer in pipes and from external surfaces. Design of heat exchangers. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257, PHYS 203 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257, PHYS 203 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280

courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Review of principles, compressible flow, potential flow, simple laminar viscous flow, boundary layers, flow around bluff bodies. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of MATH 255 or MATH 256 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280 and one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257, PHYS 203. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of MATH 255 or MATH 256 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280 and one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257, PHYS 203

courses.title: Manufacturing Processes
courses.description: Manufacturing characteristics of materials and their control. Metal forming processes, plastic deformations, rolling, forging, drawing, extrusion, sheet metal forming. Machining processes and machine tools, turning, milling, drilling, grinding. Metal fabrication, welding and casting. An introduction to process planning. [2-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Professionalism and Ethics in Engineering
courses.description: Professionalism, ethical frameworks, decolonization, equity, diversity, inclusion, law. Obligations of the engineer. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in B.A.Sc. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Lectures and readings on specialized topics of current interest in Mechanical Engineering. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Air Pollution, Technology and Society
courses.description: Causes and effects of air pollution in the context of technology and society. Topics include: impact of air pollutants on air quality and climate, atmospheric science, public policy, collective action, environmental justice, science communication, economic externalities, and ethical engineering design. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. [3-0-0]. Prerequisite: Second-year standing. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering in Society and Technological Stewardship
courses.description: Societal influences that affect engineering activities, including interactions between engineering and the economic, health, safety, legal, and cultural aspects of society; uncertainties in the prediction of such interactions; industrial policy; sustainable development; entrepreneurship; and environmental and technological stewardship. [3-0-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Sensors and Actuators
courses.description: Measurement of motion, stress, force, torque, temperature, flow and pressure; principles of sensors and signal conditioning methods; actuators. [ 2-2*-1] Prerequisite: All of MECH 360, MECH 463, ELEC 343. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Mechatronics System Instrumentation
courses.description: Architecture of mechatronics devices; integration of mechanical, electronics, sensors, actuators, computer and real time software systems; PLC and PC based systems; discrete and continuous automation system design. [2-2-2]. Prerequisite: MECH 366. Corequisite: MECH 420. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
courses.description: Fundamentals of MEMS (MicroElectroMechanical Systems). Microfabrication of MEMS with solid-state technology. LIGA and micro injection molding. Physics of MEMS. Operational principles of various MEMS devices. [2-3--0]. Prerequisite: One of MECH 224, ELEC 204 and all of MECH 360, MECH 368. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: One of MECH 224, ELEC 204 and all of MECH 360, MECH 368

courses.title: Mechatronic Product Design
courses.description: Design of mechatronic systems for industrial and human-centric applications compliant structures; electronic circuits to interface with sensors and actuators; embedded systems; precision timing and control; data acquisition and processing; user interfaces; and product innovation. [1-3-4] Prerequisite: All of MECH 366, ELEC 302, CPEN 312. and 4th year standing. Corequisite: CPEN 333, MECH 421. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: All of MECH 366, ELEC 302, CPEN 312. and 4th year standing

courses.title: Mechanical Design
courses.description: Design of shafts and welded joints. Fatigue and fracture considerations in design: failure types, failure under static and dynamic loading, fatigue failure, crack initiation, and propagation. Introduction to the FEM in mechanical design. Students can only receive credit for one of MECH 326 or MECH 426. [2-0-3] Prerequisite: One of MECH 223, MECH 260. Corequisite: MECH 360. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Data Analysis
courses.description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Economics
courses.description: Discounted cash flows. Sources of funds, cost of capital. Effects of depreciation, taxes, inflation. Evaluation and comparison of economic models for engineering projects. Replacement decisions. Public project analysis. Risk analysis. Project control, inventory analysis, simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Biofluids
courses.description: Review of principles, Navier-Stokes equations, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in human body. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 433 or MECH 533. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of MATH 255, MATH 256 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. Equivalency: MECH 533. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of MATH 255, MATH 256 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280

courses.title: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
courses.description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Muscle and joint loads. Muscle mechanics. Musculoskeletal dynamics. Gait. Tissue mechanics of tendon, ligament, articular cartilage, and bone. Biomaterials. Application examples in orthopaedics including joint replacement and fracture fixation. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 435 or MECH 535. Students who have received credit for BMEG 230 or 330 cannot also receive credit for MECH 435. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 221 or (b) all of APSC 278, MECH 260. Equivalency: MECH 535. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 221 or (b) all of APSC 278, MECH 260

courses.title: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
courses.description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, spine, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets. Recommended pre-requisites: MECH 224, or all of MECH 260 and BMEG 330. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 436 or MECH 536. [3-0-1]. Equivalency: MECH 536. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
courses.recommended: MECH 224, or all of MECH 260 and BMEG 330

courses.title: Biomechanics Research
courses.description: Seminar in Biomechanics research. [1-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fuel Cell Systems
courses.description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion: fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Recommended prerequisites: MECH 327 and MECH 375. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 445 or MECH 577. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. Equivalency: MECH 577. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Advanced Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Mechanics of rubber, tissue, and gels at large viscoelastic deformation; large plastic deformations and damage of materials; mechanical characterization of materials (property extraction from mechanical tests); selected problems in linear elasticity. [3-0-1] Prerequisite: MECH 360 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametric elements. Development of computer programs for simple problems. Utilization of existing computer packages. Application to mechanical engineering problems. Recommended prerequisite: MECH 360. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 462 or MECH 514. [2-3*-0] Prerequisite: One of MECH 224 or MECH 260. Equivalency: MECH 514. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Mechanical Vibrations
courses.description: Theory of vibration of mechanical systems. Undamped 1 degree of freedom vibration, forced vibrations and resonance, damping, multiple degree of freedom systems, mode shapes and orthogonality, continuous systems, vibration measuring instruments and frequency spectrum analysis.[3-2*-1] Prerequisite: One of MECH 224, MECH 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Industrial Robotics
courses.description: Definition and classification of industrial robotic devices. Selection and implementation issues. Workcell environments. Forward and inverse kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning. Sensing and manipulation tasks. Control architectures. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 466 or MECH 467. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC 442, EECE 571R, EECE 589, MECH 464 or MECH 563. [3-0-1]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Control Systems I
courses.description: Introduction to control systems: system modelling and transfer functions; block diagrams; principles of feedback; stability; Bode plots; root locus methods; frequency response; control design. Laboratory experiments to support the lecture content. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 466, ELEC 341, or MECH 467. [3-1-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) all of MECH 220, MECH 224 or (b) MATH 255 and one of ELEC 201, ELEC 202, ELEC 204, EECE 251, EECE 253; or (c) all of ELEC 204, ELEC 221, ENPH 270, MATH 255. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) all of MECH 220, MECH 224 or (b) MATH 255 and one of ELEC 201, ELEC 202, ELEC 204, EECE 251, EECE 253; or (c) all of ELEC 204, ELEC 221, ENPH 270, MATH 255

courses.title: Computer Control of Mechatronics Systems
courses.description: Block diagrams and transfer functions, continuous and discrete domain transformations, feedback control system characteristics, control design in both continuous and discrete domain, absolute and relative stability, laboratory examples of Mechatronic systems design. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 467 or MECH 541. Credit cannot be obtained for both MECH 466 and MECH 467. [3-2*-2] Prerequisite: One of MECH 366, MANU 386. Equivalency: MECH 541. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Control Systems II
courses.description: Introduction to state space control methods for linear systems including modal control, controllability, observability, linear quadratic regulators, optimal control. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 366. Prerequisite: MECH 466, ELEC 341, or CHBE 356. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 468 or MECH 509. [3-0-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Dynamic System Modelling
courses.description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal systems; analytical models; model representations such as linear and bond graphs; response analysis; digital simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Energy Conversion Systems
courses.description: Energy supply and demand. Energy conversion chain. Electrical power generation using thermal power plants, renewable energy, and fuel cells. Rankine cycle steam power. Brayton cycle gas turbine power plants, intercooling, reheat, and regeneration. Internal combustion engines. Exhaust gas after treatment. Combined and binary cycles. Nuclear power. Recommended pre-requisites: All of MECH 327, MECH 375. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280

courses.title: An Introduction to Pulp and Papermaking
courses.description: Overview of pulp and paper operations. Conversion of wood to fibre through mechanical or chemical pulping, processing of recycled fibre, the papermaking process and paper converting operations. Contemporary developments. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning
courses.description: Principles of air conditioning; psychometrics and refrigeration. Heat transfer through building materials. Estimation of heating and cooling loads including the use of current software. System design. Ground, air and water source heat pumps. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: MECH 375. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Aerospace Propulsion
courses.description: Cycle analysis of jet engines, thermodynamic cycles, mechanics and thermodynamics of combustion, components and the performance characteristics of chemical rockets. The detailed analysis of operating characteristics of turbojet, turbofan, turboprop, afterburning, and ramjet propulsion systems. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: All of MECH 327, MECH 375, MECH 380. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power, and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Engine emission and control systems. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH 327. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 478 or MECH 578. [3-0-0]. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280. Equivalency: MECH 578. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280

courses.title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Techniques for numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, including an introduction to the finite difference, finite volume and finite element approaches. Simulation of laminar and turbulent flows, including common turbulent models. Validation techniques. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH 380. [3-1-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
courses.description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 481 or MECH 581. [3-1*-0] Prerequisite: MECH 380 Equivalency: MECH 581 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Aircraft Stability and Control
courses.description: Basics of subsonic flight in the atmosphere; aircraft performance, stability and control, loading and air worthiness. Detailed example. [2-0-2] Corequisite: MECH 481 or MECH 581. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Aircraft Design: Structures
courses.description: Structural components of aircraft, introduction to the finite element method, bending and buckling of thin plates. Design of aircraft wing and fuselage structures, moments of inertia for complex shapes. [3-0-1]. Prerequisite: One of MECH 224, MECH 260. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Ship Design
courses.description: This course introduces the ship design process from a Systems Engineering point of view. Topics include ship operational requirements, space and weight estimation, parametric design, optimization techniques, and the impacts of ship design on economics and the environment. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 486 or NAME 581. [3-0-0] Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 380 or (b) CIVL 315. Corequisite: All of MECH 488, CIVL 435. Equivalency: NAME 581 This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Ship Hydrodynamics
courses.description: Ship terminology, lines plans, ship hydrostatics, transverse and longitudinal stability of ships, dimensional analysis, ship resistance prediction; ship propulsion methods, propeller selection and design. Recommended prerequisites: One of MECH 380_V or CIVL 315_V, or enrollment in the NAME MEng or NAME MEL program. Prerequisite: One of MECH 225, MECH 280, or CIVL 215. [3-0-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: One of MECH 225, MECH 280, or CIVL 215

courses.recommended: One of MECH 380_V or CIVL 315_V, or enrollment in the NAME MEng or NAME MEL program

courses.title: Experimental Thermofluids
courses.description: Experimental uncertainty. Design of experiments. Test facilities. Temperature and pressure measurement techniques and instrumentation. Velocity and flow rate measurement techniques. Flow visualization. Case studies of industrial and research experimental practice. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 489 or MECH 582. [3-2-0]. Prerequisite: All of MECH 375, MECH 380. Equivalency: MECH 582. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary CapstoneDesign Project
courses.description: An extension to projects in the New Venture Design Program that introduces additional technical design principles and requirements. Registration for this program is only permitted for Mechanical Engineering students who are in the New Venture Design Program. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 490, MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, or MECH 459. Restricted to students with only fourth-year standing in Mechanical Engineering. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 328, MECH 360. [1-0- 1]; [1-0-1] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Computer-Aided Manufacturing
courses.description: NC programming and machining with interactive CAD/CAM systems. Curve and surface geometry for tool-path generation. Tool-path generation methodologies. Geometric modelling techniques for simulation and verification of manufacturing processes. Introduction to Computer-Aided Process Planning. Supplementary tutorial laboratory experiments. Recommended co- requisites: MECH 392 or MANU 380. Prerequisite: MECH 224 or MECH 260. [2-2-0] This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Academic Research I
courses.description: Research project directed by a faculty member in Mechanical Engineering. [0-5-1]. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

prereq.text: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor

tree.other: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor

courses.title: Academic Research II
courses.description: Additional research project directed by a faculty member in Mechanical Engineering. [0-5-1] Prerequisite: MECH 493 and permission of instructor. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Industrial Engineering
courses.description: Organizational structure. Manufacturing systems and group technology. Classification and coding. Scheduling and sequencing of operations. Forecasting. Quality control for variables and attributes. Plant location. System reliability analysis. Advanced manufacturing automation concepts. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Management
courses.description: Organization structures. Management styles. Cost systems and control. Financial statements; accounting procedures. Budgets and performance control. Project management. Human resources management. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Skills and Data Analysis
courses.description: Research environment, funding and dissemination systems; literature reviews and critically evaluating papers; creating research questions; research ethics, data security and research records; equity, diversity, and inclusion in research. Recommended pre-requisite: Third-year standing. [3-0-0]. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Communication
courses.description: Scholarly writing and communication in engineering. Standard research genres such as journal articles, conference posters, and grant proposals. Students will write on the topic of their CREATE-U research. [2-0-2]. Prerequisite: MECH 497. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Thermodynamic principles, Maxwell relations, availability, irreversibility, and equilibrium. Introduction to statistical mechanics. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Governing equations; viscous incompressible flow, incompressible potential flow; incompressible boundary layers, stability and turbulence; compressible potential flow. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Linear Elasticity
courses.description: Stress and strain in three dimensions, fundamental field equations of linear elasticity; equilibrium, compatibility, Hooke's law; Papkovitch-Neuber solution, plane stress and plane strain; torsion, torsion of thin-walled members with warping restraint; plate theory. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Linear Vibrations
courses.description: Transient and steady state vibration analysis of continuous and discrete mechanical systems. Lagrange's equation and Hamilton's Principle. Measurement of vibration. Machinery health monitoring. Frequency domain analysis. Experimental modal analysis. Vibration of rotating machinery. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Analytical Dynamics
courses.description: Newtonian mechanics; generalized co-ordinates and analytical mechanics; Lagrange equations; Hamilton's Principle; rotational motion and rigid body dynamics; Gyroscopic motion; phase space, equilibrium, and stability of motion; stability characteristics of autonomous systems; Hamilton-Jacobi method; applications. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Controls
courses.description: State space model; stability; controlability; observability; Kalman decomposition; state feedback; observer; linear quadratic regulator; Kalman filter. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 468 or MECH 509. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Experimental Methods in Mechanics
courses.description: Operating principles of transducers for measuring typical quantities; the construction of transducers and factors controlling their measurement accuracy; electronic signal conditioning equipment and computerized data acquisition system. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Linear FEA in Solids and Heat Transfer
courses.description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametic elements. Computer program development. Utilization of existing computer packages. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 514 or MECH 462. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Applied Mechanics
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Control Sensors and Actuators
courses.description: Review of control, instrumentation and design. Performance specification of control components, component matching, error analysis. Operating principles, analysis, modelling, design considerations of control sensors and actuators such as analog sensors for motion measurement, digital transducers, stepper motors, DC motors, induction motors, synchronous motors, and hydraulic actuators. Control techniques pertaining to actuators. Applications. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Microelectromechanical Systems
courses.description: Micro-fabrication of MEMS: solid-state technology and other micromachining techniques. Engineering principles of various MEMS devices. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Software Development for Mechatronic Systems
courses.description: Equivalency: EECE 524. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Instrumentation for Mechatronic Systems
courses.description: Equivalency: EECE 525. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Mechatronic System Design Project I
courses.description: The design, analysis, manufacturability, instrumentation and computer control of a selected dynamic machinery assembly will be studied. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Mechatronic System Design Project II
courses.description: The full assembly, instrumentation, computer and electronic interfacing, and testing of a dynamic machine. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Modelling of Dynamic Systems
courses.description: Advanced modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, thermal and multi-domain systems; inter-domain analogies; analytical models in time and frequency domains; modelling tools; response analysis; digital simulation; practical project. Recommended pre-requisite: prior undergraduate coursework in dynamics, vibration, or electrical circuits. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
courses.recommended: prior undergraduate coursework in dynamics, vibration, or electrical circuits

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Biomedical Engineering
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Biofluids
courses.description: Principles, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in the human body. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 433 or MECH 533. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
courses.description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Static and dynamic analysis of the musculoskeletal system. Gait. Musculoskeletal tissue mechanics. Biomaterials. Advanced study of relevant problems in orthopaedics, including joint replacement, fracture fixation, and spinal disorders. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 435 or MECH 535. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
courses.description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 436 or MECH 536. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Mechatronics, Manufacturing, Controls, and Automation
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Computer Control of Multi-Axis Machines
courses.description: Digital control laws for servo drives; state space and transfer function models of feed drives; tracking errors; trajectory generation of multi-axis machines; contouring analysis of multi-axes servo drives; real time linear and circular interpolation methods supported by laboratory applications. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 467 or MECH 541. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: CAD/CAM Principles and Practice
courses.description: 3D geometric modelling; parametric representation of curves and surfaces; CNC machine tool programming; milling operations and setup; tool path generation for three- and five-axis sculptured surface machining. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Machine Tool Structures and Vibrations
courses.description: Review of metal cutting mechanics, milling, static deformations of machine tools. Machine tool vibrations, forced and self-excited vibrations in machining, chatter, stability. Sensors for machine tool monitoring and adaptive control. Sensor assisted intelligent machining techniques. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Writing
courses.description: Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 498 or MECH 556. Equivalency: MECH 500X, MECH 500A, MECH 550U This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Skills for Engineers
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Professional Responsibility for Engineers
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Engineering Project Management Fundamentals
courses.description: Students who have taken NAME 524 are not eligible to receive credit for this course. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Multivariable Feedback Control
courses.description: Well-posedness and internal stability of feedback systems, performance limitations, uncertainty, LFT representations, robust stability and robust performance, model reduction, linear matrix inequalities, H- infinity control, multi-objective control, mu-analysis and synthesis, H-infinity gain- scheduling, control applications. Recommended prerequisite: MECH 466, MECH 468, ELEC 341 or equivalent. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 562, EECE 508, or ELEC 572. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Robotics: Kinematics, Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Definitions and classification Kinematics: homogeneous transformations, manipulator kinematic equations, forward and inverse kinematic solution methods, differential kinematic equations, motion trajectories. Dynamics: Lagrange-Euler formulations, Newton-Euler formulation. Control: methods, robot control hierarchy, control of single joint and multiple link manipulators, advanced control methods. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC 442, EECE 571R, EECE 589, MECH 464, or MECH 563. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, and Heat Transfer
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Convection Heat Transfer
courses.description: Governing equations for laminar and turbulent flow. Forced convection in internal and external flow. Free, and combined free and forced convection. Heat transfer at high velocities, in rarefied gases and in two-phase flow. Mass transfer. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Combustion
courses.description: Thermodynamics of combustion, stoichiometry, heat of formation and reaction. Equilibrium composition and adiabatic flame temperature. Chemical kinetics of combustion. Flames in premixed gases; laminar and turbulent flame propagation. Diffusion flames, pollutant emissions and combustion in IC engines. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fuel Cell Systems
courses.description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion; fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 445 or MECH 577. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Numerical engine modelling and analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 478 or MECH 578. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
courses.description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 581 or MECH 481. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Experimental Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Modelling Test facilities. Wind tunnel force measurement. Theory of conventional and modern manometry. Classical velocimetry. Hotwire anemometry. Theory and application of laser Doppler velocimetry. Particle image velocimetry. Flow visualization techniques. Thermometry. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 489 or MECH 582. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Fluid-Structure Interaction
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Turbulent Shear Flow
courses.description: The basic equations of fluid motion; introduction to hydro-dynamic stability; Reynolds' equations; energy equations for turbulent motion; intermittency; similarity near a solid boundary and in free turbulence; approximate methods for predicting the growth of turbulent boundary layers and free symmetrical shear flows. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Analytical, computational, and experimental methods in fluid mechanics. Overview of CFD program development. Finite volume methods, spacial discretization and spatial accuracy analysis. Boundary conditions. Time advance methods, time accuracy, and stability. Application to model problems and to the incompressible laminar Navier-Stokes equations. Validation techniques for CFD codes. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Selected advanced topics in CFD, typically chosen from: Finite volume methods on curvilinear meshes and structured mesh generation. Finite volume methods on unstructured meshes. Multigrid methods for elliptic PDE's. Reynolds-averaged form of the Navier-Stokes equations and turbulence modelling. Three-dimensional flows. Compressible flows. Prerequisite: One of MECH 510, MECH 587. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Special advanced lecture courses may be arranged for graduate students upon the approval of the department head. There will not be more than 6 credits in any one such course. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Directed Studies in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Project for M.Eng. Studies
courses.description: Project on assigned topic of specialization. For students registered in the M.Eng. program whose project is supervised by a faculty member in the department of Mechanical Engineering. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Current topics in mechanical engineering research for M.A.Sc. students. Pass/Fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: For M.A.Sc. Pass/Fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Emerging Topics in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Current topics in mechanical engineering for doctoral students. Pass/Fail. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

courses.title: Doctoral Dissertation
courses.description: Pass/Fail This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
